title: Route outbound HTTP through the centralized client

facts.note: Derived from the layer segment in the file path. Integration is excluded (the client's own home); files with no layer segment are out of scope.
Any non-test source file outside vendored/build directories, whether newly written, edited, or untouched-but-in-scope. No diff condition: existing bare calls are in scope too.

Preventive signal: the task involves outbound HTTP from a consumer layer. Fires before any code is written; not a precondition when the layer/file_kind facts already match a file containing a bare call.
Alternative trigger only (not required): a detector finding on any in-scope file, including pre-existing bare calls.

fires: An application-layer use case needs data from an upstream service and the agent is about to write the call.
A presentation-layer server handler already contains `axios(...)` to load data for the fragment it renders.
A domain module calls `fetch()` to look up a remote value.
doesNotFire: An integration-layer adapter or the centralized HTTP client itself calls `fetch()`.
A test file calls `fetch()` against a test server.
A file in a vendored or build directory contains `fetch(`.
A file whose path carries no layer segment calls `fetch()`.
`fetch(` appears only inside a string or comment (masked source).

given: A source file in the domain, application or presentation layer performs, or needs to perform, outbound HTTP
when: the agent writes, edits or is responsible for that file
then: Make outbound HTTP through the project's centralized, contract-driven client (integration-layer client/adapter), never via platform `fetch()` or bare `axios`.
prefer: Use the existing integration-layer HTTP client or adapter.
Let that boundary own transport concerns: headers, retries, decoding, error translation.
During GREEN: make only the outbound call and mapping the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: reuse an existing client or port before a new abstraction; if no compliant boundary exists, add the smallest integration adapter the behavior requires.
avoid: Calling `fetch()`/`axios` directly just to make the test pass.
A generalized HTTP framework for hypothetical endpoints.
Migrating unrelated HTTP callers beyond the one the current acceptance touches.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories (never scanned).
Files with no layer segment (outside the rule).
why: The centralized client holds retries, timeouts, auth headers, tracing and error translation; a bare fetch has none and never acquires them because nobody remembers it exists. In htmx apps a bare server-side fetch behind a rendered fragment fails as a blank swap the user sees.
evidence: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no bare `fetch(`/`axios(` in domain/, application/ or presentation/ files of the affected source (the affected source satisfies this boundary rule).
The outbound call in the change is made via the integration-layer client/adapter (or a port implemented there).
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_clean_architecture_detector (validator). Flags a bare `fetch(` or `axios(` call in consumer layers domain/, application/, presentation/, scanning masked source (strings/comments masked out).
Integration layer is excluded — it is the centralized client's own home.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Terms: centralized_client = the project's contract-driven HTTP client, where retries, timeouts, auth headers, tracing and error translation live; bare_primitive = a direct `fetch(` or `axios(` in a consumer layer — a call site with none of those, which will not acquire them because nobody remembers it exists.
Source fix_hint headings: 'Canonical path:', 'During GREEN:', 'Do not broaden:', 'Prove:'.

sharedNodes.text: During GREEN: make only the change required by the current acceptance; reuse an existing compliant boundary before introducing another abstraction; if none exists, add the smallest one the behavior requires. Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes and the affected source satisfies the rule.

Layers are identified by a path segment: domain/, application/, presentation/ (consumer layers) and integration/ (home of transport adapters and the centralized HTTP client). A file carrying no layer segment is outside layer rules rather than in violation of them.
